close_reason: Positive observation, no action required. ChangeRecord-with-snapshot pattern at memory.rs:136-141 (capturing related_type + type_name at mutation time) is the right design for enabling destroyed-array filtering. Closing as 'noted, what good looks like'.
description:
Why this is good: The ChangeRecord struct (memory.rs:136-141) carries related_type and type_name as String fields, captured at create/update/destroy time. This makes get_metadata_changes able to filter the destroyed array CORRECTLY even though destroyed objects no longer exist in the objects map.

The alternative (which would be 'simpler') is to store only Ids in ChangeRecord and re-fetch the object via objects map at filter time. That doesn't work for destroyed entries because the object is gone. The current design pays a small RAM cost (two extra strings per change log entry) to enable strict §3.3 destroyed-array filtering.

The rustdoc on the field (memory.rs:128-141) explicitly explains why these strings are populated at push time. The destroy_object impl (memory.rs:872-890) captures the snapshot BEFORE the value moves into the map.

A future contributor might suggest 'drop these fields, re-fetch from objects at filter time' to save RAM. Defend: it cannot work for destroyed entries. The current design is correct.

Cross-reference: tests/metadata_tests.rs:510 (changes_filter_drops_non_matching_destroyed) is the regression test for this design.
title: ChangeRecord-with-snapshot pattern in memory.rs:136-141 — captures (related_type, type_name) AT mutation time so destroyed-array filtering works
